items.title: Looking for contributors 🧑‍💻
items.body:
Hey everyone 👋  

I’m building **AI Audit Shelf** — a lightweight, open‑source system that brings **Git‑like versioning to AI workflows**.  

Right now the project is early, working, and ready for contributions from people who care about:

- AI agent observability  
- local‑first tooling  
- clean, minimal codebases (FastAPI + SQLite + Vanilla JS)

***

### What AI Audit Shelf does (very short)

Every AI action becomes an **immutable chapter**.  
Chapters are bundled into **versioned books** on a **shelf** grouped by feature.  

For example:

```txt
Library
  └── [Feature: HR Automation]
        ├── b_001 v1 Employee Onboarding
        └── b_002 v2 Employee Onboarding
             ↑ full audit trail preserved
```

The goal:  
Make AI workflows **auditable, versioned, and reproducible** — not just vibes and screenshots.

***

### Where help is needed

I’m looking for contributors in areas like:

- **Features & UX**  
  - New CLI commands  
  - Better filters / search in the dashboard  
  - Export formats (e.g., PDF, CSV, YAML)

- **Integrations**  
  - More examples for:  
    - LangChain  
    - OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini patterns  
    - RAG pipelines  
    - shell scripts, services, etc.

- **Testing & docs**  
  - Adding tests (pytest, fixtures, edge cases)  
  - Writing guides:  
    - “How to plug AI Audit Shelf into your existing agent”  
    - “How to debug a regression using diffs”

- **Dev‑infra**  
  - GitHub Actions (CI, linting, tests)  
  - Better release notes / changelog automation  
  - Docker setup (optional, non‑required)

***

### How to get started

1. **Fork** the repo:  
   https://github.com/ATHARVA262005/ai-audit-shelf  

2. Find an issue labeled:  
   - `good first issue`  
   - `help wanted`  
   or just open a **discussion** if you have an idea.

3. Drop a comment here or in a new issue saying:  
   - what you’d like to work on  
   - your preferred area (CLI, dashboard, integrations, docs, infra)

4. I’ll help you scope it and answer any questions.

***

### No‑pressure rules

- You don’t need to be an expert.  
- You can contribute small: a typo, one test, one example.  
- If you’re new to open source, I’ll walk you through the PR flow.

***

If this looks interesting, **comment below** with:

- “I’d like to help with [area]”  
or  
- “I have an idea for [feature]”

Let’s make AI workflows **auditable by default** together. 🚀  

***

items.title: Looking for contributors!
items.body:
We're looking for contributors who will help us to provide Swift and JVM (Java/Kotlin) langage bindings for the project. This is a paid offer - you have an opportunity to work on OSS project and get paid for that! :) We have an [open collective organization](https://opencollective.com/y-collective) to handle necessary payments.

We're looking for developers who are well versed with the standards of the languages they are going to provide bindings for - naming conventions and patterns, package management, automated tests and CI/CD integration via Github Action directly on the project page. Of course having some experience with building C interop layer for these languages and managing quirks of crossing managed/unmanaged memory layer is very valuable.

The work can be realized by calling the Rust library directly via special macro libraries - this is how ywasm, [ypy](https://github.com/y-crdt/ypy) and [yrb](https://github.com/y-crdt/yrb) came to live - or by using yffi project (which exposes yrs via C FII). I've noticed existing projects like [swift-bridge](https://github.com/chinedufn/swift-bridge) and [jni](https://docs.rs/jni/latest/jni/) but their maturity for this project purposes needs to be evaluated.

/cc @dmonad

items.title: RFC: Rewriting pam_usb in Rust for Memory Safety & Modernization (Looking for Contributors!)
items.body: Originally posted by **mcdope** May 22, 2026 **The Context** As the maintainer of pam_usb, I spend a lot of time thinking about the long-term security and maintainability of this project. PAM modules sit at the absolute core of system authentication. A single memory bug here can easily lead to privilege escalation or a complete denial of service. Recent rigorous security audits of our legacy C codebase—leveraging advanced AI-driven vulnerability research—have uncovered a significant number of CVEs. While these specific issues are being addressed, the fundamental problem remains: C is inherently risky for this kind of low-level, high-stakes system integration. **The Vision & Roadmap** I believe pam_usb is the perfect candidate for a complete Rust rewrite, similar to what the sudo-rs project has achieved. *Please note on timing:* We haven't even reached the 1.0.0 milestone for the current C codebase yet. This rewrite is a long-term strategic goal and would be targeted for pam_usb v2.0 at the earliest. The goals for this v2.0 rewrite would be: * **Zero Memory Unsafety:** Eliminate buffer overflows, use-after-free, and memory leaks by design. * **Modernized Config & Migration Path:** Ditch our legacy XML configuration in favor of something sane and modern like TOML or YAML. *Crucially, this must include a migration mechanism (or standalone tool) to smoothly convert existing XML configurations on systems where pam_usb is already installed.* * **Robust Hardware Detection:** Leverage modern crates to interact directly with udev for fast and reliable USB event handling. * **Better Error Handling:** Take advantage of Rust's Result type so we never accidentally swallow a critical hardware or PAM API error again. **The Setup: How we could work together** I am not a Rust developer, but I know the PAM ecosystem and this domain inside out. I am looking for motivated Rust engineers to lead the code architecture and implementation. *What I bring to the table:* * Deep knowledge of PAM edge-cases, systemd, and polkit interactions. * A proven methodology for AI-assisted security auditing. (Full disclosure: the recent CVEs were discovered by heavily prompting LLMs like Claude to do the heavy lifting in vulnerability research. I will apply this exact same aggressive testing pipeline to the new Rust codebase.) * Management of cross-distribution packaging requirements (ensuring the new Rust binaries will actually build and ship cleanly on Debian, Fedora, and Arch. Ideally plus NixOS). * Code review focusing on logical security and system integration. *What you bring:* * Rust expertise to design a safe, idiomatic, and maintainable codebase. * Drive to build the FFI bindings to PAM and wire up the hardware detection logic. **Scope of the Rewrite** For the sake of completeness and maintainability, the goal is to port the *entire* tool suite, avoiding a fragmented codebase. We would need to replace all existing components: 1. pam_usb.so (The actual PAM module - requires C FFI) 2. pamusb-conf (CLI tool to manage configuration) 3. pamusb-check (CLI tool to verify authentication) 4. pamusb-agent (Daemon for automatic locking/unlocking desktop sessions) 5. ...and any other auxiliary tools or scripts currently in the repository. **Next Steps** If you are an experienced Rustacean looking for a high-impact, security-focused open-source project, I would love to hear your thoughts. * Does this sound feasible? * Which crates would you suggest for the PAM bindings and udev interaction? * What would this mean for crosscompiling to armhf, arm64, i386 and m68k? Let's discuss the architecture below! (Kinda relates to #55)

items.title: State of framework & looking for contributors!!
items.body:
Hi there, many of you already know me, but I am the original creator and lead-maintainer of TPPDF.

I started the project in 2016 as I was in need of creating PDFs in a recipe management app. Over the years I continued working on TPPDF, even tough said app doesn't even exist anymore.

Ever since then I unfortunately never had a real use case in my projects again. Therefore working on the framework is mostly done next to other projects and time is rather scarce. I do enjoy working on TPPDF, as I believe this sophisticated, free PDF generation solution should have existed way earlier than when I started working on it.

Now that I only have limited time to invest, I am asking *YOU*, all active users/contributors of this framework, to help me out:

- Please, open up more issues if you encounter new bugs.
- Please, comment/mark duplicate issues, so I can close them and keep a clean state.
- Please, add as much information as possible when opening up issues. Especially a working code example any developer can download, test and directly reproduce the issue makes it way easier to invest time.
- Please, (if possible) let me know you are using the project/add your app to the [list](https://github.com/techprimate/TPPDF#apps-using-tppdf). It keeps any developer (not only myself) more motivated to keep working, as it is almost impossible to track, how many users actually use/rely on the framework.

...and also most importantly:

- Please, create **Pull-Requests**! If I don't find the time to investigate an issue, but you already found a solution, let me know in the comments. I will review all code, so we can keep the quality and I will give feedback to your contribution. If necessary we will start a discussion, to get the most out of it. (FYI, there is no bad code, just different levels of experience. So don't worry too much about that). Also a big help is clarifying method names and documentation!

I also want you to know, that we are not developing TPPDF to be a commercial solution (only derivatives of it), but instead because of our believes in Open Source software. As it hardly generates any money, I can't give it the highest priority and only work on it on the side of my every-day tasks. 

### I am very thankful to anyone who has donated before, or will in the future! No matter how much, I always have and always will see it as a token of appreciation, and be grateful! ❤️

If you have a time-critical issue or a need of consulting, that should to be resolved in a closer future, I can give you professional paid support, so please reach out to me either on Twitter [@philprimes](https://twitter.com/philprimes) or on our website [techprimate.com](https://techprimate.com/contact).

Hopefully this gives you a little more insight in what's going on, and why the development of the framework seems to be stale.

Thank you so much for your understanding!

Best regards,

Phil

items.title: Help wanted: production Android release and Google Play readiness

labels.name: store-readiness
labels.description: Google Play and App Store release preparation

items.body:
Solphivia has a working Android community alpha. We are looking for Android contributors to help turn it into a maintainable, tested release suitable for Google Play.

First contribution: inspect the current Java app and propose a short migration plan before a large refactor.

Deliverables:
- [ ] Migrate compile/target SDK from 35 to the applicable Play requirement (currently API 36 for new mobile submissions); document behavior changes.
- [ ] Review overlay and foreground-service lifecycle, permissions, battery use and background restrictions.
- [ ] Add a reproducible signed AAB procedure with signing keys kept outside the repository.
- [ ] Prepare privacy/Data safety disclosures, AI-response reporting, accessibility and store-review evidence.
- [ ] Define a device matrix and internal/closed testing plan appropriate to the developer account.

Done means a reproducible release candidate and documented remaining submission blockers, not a promise of store approval. No developer-account access or signing credentials are needed to contribute to this issue.

References: [Google Play target API](https://developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk), [testing requirements](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/14151465).

Comment with the part you would like to take on and a small first step. Italian and English are welcome. This is a community collaboration request, not an advertised paid position. Code is MIT; character/artwork rights remain reserved.

items.title: [Show HN] InvoiceBot — Open-source invoicing for freelancers, zero dependencies
items.body:
## What I Built

**InvoiceBot** — a complete invoicing SaaS for freelancers built with zero npm dependencies. One `node server.js` and you're live.

### The Problem
Every invoicing tool is either too complex (built for enterprises), too expensive ($30-50/month), or too locked-in (your data on their servers). Freelancers just need to create an invoice, send it, and get paid.

### The Solution
A single Node.js server — no dependencies, no build step, no framework — that does invoicing and nothing else.

**What's working right now:**
- Dashboard with real-time revenue tracking (paid, pending, overdue)
- Invoice CRUD with line items and auto tax calculation
- Client management
- Invoice preview + print/PDF export
- Stripe checkout integration (clients pay online)
- Subscription billing for SaaS model
- One-click deploy to Railway, Render, Fly.io, or Docker
- Dark mode, mobile responsive

**The numbers:**
- 0 dependencies
- ~1,200 lines of code
- 30 seconds to first invoice
- < 2 minutes to deploy
- $0-7/month hosting cost

### Business Model
- Free tier: 3 invoices/month
- Pro ($19/mo): Unlimited everything + Stripe payments
- Business ($39/mo): Multi-currency, recurring, reports, API

22 Pro subscribers = $5,000 ARR. That's the whole plan.

### Tech Stack
Node.js (stdlib only) + Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS + JSON storage + Stripe

### Try It
```bash
git clone https://github.com/abuadamalmaliki-prog/B00K.git
cd B00K && node server.js
```

Looking for feedback, contributors, and early users. Star if this is useful!
